frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/settings/pages/SessionsPage.tsx:84 — `const sessions = (sessionsQuery.data?.sessions ?? []) as unknown as SessionRow[];` uses a double `as unknown as` cast across the API boundary. getAuthApi().listSessions() already returns ListSessionsResponse whose `sessions: SessionInfo[]` (frontend/packages/api-client/src/auth/types.ts:135-155) is structurally identical to the local SessionRow (id, deviceInfo, ipAddress, userAgent, createdAt, lastUsedAt, isCurrent), so the cast is unnecessary AND strips compile-time type-checking.

Latent risk: the cast defeats drift detection on a security control. If the backend SessionInfo DTO ever renames a field (e.g. isCurrent -> is_current), TypeScript would no longer flag it; at SessionsPage.tsx:85 `sessions.some((s) => !s.isCurrent)` would read undefined, making `hasOtherSessions` always true and silently breaking the 'revoke all other sessions' logout control. Fix: drop the cast (the types are assignable) or map explicitly from SessionInfo -> SessionRow so a mismatch fails the build.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/compliance/pages/ContentModerationPage.tsx:126-192 — handleTakeAction and handleDecideAppeal collect free-text via window.prompt() and cast it unchecked to a literal union before sending to the moderation API: `action_type: actionType as 'remove' | 'restrict' | 'warn' | 'approve'` (line 143) and `decision: decision as 'uphold' | 'overturn'` (line 179). Any typed string (e.g. 'delet', 'Approve', '') that passes the truthiness guard is coerced to a valid-looking union member and POSTed with no client-side validation — the compliance/moderation action is only as safe as the backend's own validation.

Same handlers hardcode user-facing English strings in alert()/window.prompt() ('Enter action type (remove, restrict, warn, approve):', 'Failed to take action. Please try again.', etc.) — the app is react-i18next-enabled but this page wraps none of them in t(), so these moderator-facing messages are untranslatable (i18n gap). Both issues are acknowledged Phase-1 stubs (TODO(Phase-2) at lines 128, 167 to replace window.prompt with a validated modal form), but the unvalidated-union cast is a correctness/security-adjacent gap worth closing when the modal lands.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/util/url_validator.rs:145-164 — validate_fetch_url()'s Host::Ipv6 branch only rejects is_loopback(), fc00::/7 and fe80::/10. It does NOT reject IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals (::ffff:a.b.c.d) nor IPv4-compatible/unspecified forms, so https://[::ffff:169.254.169.254]/ parses as Host::Ipv6 with segments[0]==0 (no rule matches, is_loopback()==false) and passes validation — a direct SSRF bypass to the cloud metadata endpoint. Same gap lets ::ffff:127.0.0.1, ::ffff:10.x.x.x and ::ffff:192.168.x.x reach loopback/private targets that the IPv4 branch (lines 93-144) is careful to block.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/agency_imports.rs:237-241 and 289-293 — test_connection and run_import (both gated only by check_agency_membership, i.e. any authenticated agency member) feed the user-supplied feed_url through validate_fetch_url as the sole SSRF guard before the import worker fetches it; the inline comment at 284-286 explicitly intends to reject 'http://169.254.169.254/', but the IPv4-mapped IPv6 form defeats that intent. Because a literal IP requires no DNS resolution, the 'worker re-validates the resolved IP' mitigation does not apply — the bypass is reachable in production.

Suggested fix: in validate_fetch_url, before the range checks, canonicalize IPv4-mapped/compatible IPv6 (ip.to_ipv4_mapped()/to_ipv4()) and run the octet checks against the embedded IPv4; also reject the IPv6/IPv4 unspecified address (::, 0.0.0.0 is already covered) and consider 100.64.0.0/10 (CGNAT) for completeness.
